edition.locus: Bd I 3-4 (ch. I, after the address)

pass_a_gloss: But also if they should belittle us and cheapen us, calling us either irreverent or stupid, those who are foreign to the dialect according to the holy writings, let us remind ourselves that the hope on hope, the one to be paid back to us after 'still a little', will be paid back through contempt of lips, through a different tongue. And who would not receive tribulation on tribulation, so that straightaway he receives also hope on hope, calculating with Paul that not worthy are the sufferings of the now time, by which as if we buy the blessedness, in relation to the glory about to be uncovered toward us from God; and most of all since the immediate lightness of our tribulation, light both being and being said for those not weighed by the things standing around, by how much more it becomes surpassing, by so much greater and more a weight of age-long glory it works out for us, if during the time of those pressing and as if wanting to squeeze our souls, having turned away our governing part from the toilsome things, we should look not at the toilsome things standing present but at those, through the endurance in these, stored up by grace of God for those who competed lawfully in Christ, he multiplying the benefactions and beyond the worth of the labours of the competitor gifting so many things as would be fitting for the great-giving God, not being stingy in reckoning and knowledgeably magnifying his own graces, to give upon those who as much as was in their power, through having looked down on the clay vessel, displayed the love with whole soul toward him.
pass_b_english: But even if those who are strangers to the language of the holy Scriptures scorn us and treat us as worthless, calling us either impious or fools, let us remind ourselves that the hope “upon hope”, which is to be given back to us in “yet a little” while, will be given back “because of the scorn of lips, by another tongue” (Isaiah 28:11). And who would not welcome “affliction upon affliction” (Isaiah 28:10) in order at once to welcome “hope upon hope” as well, reckoning with Paul that “the sufferings of the present time”, with which we as it were purchase blessedness, “are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us” (Romans 8:18) from God?

All the more so since “the momentary lightness of our affliction” (it is light, and is called light, for those who are not weighed down by what surrounds them), the more it overflows, the greater and fuller is the “weight of eternal glory” it works for us (2 Corinthians 4:17). That holds if, in the time of those who afflict us and who wish, as it were, to crush our souls, we turn our ruling faculty away from what is painful and look not at the painful things now present but at what is laid up, by the grace of God, for those who have contended “lawfully” in Christ (2 Timothy 2:5), because of their endurance in these things. For God multiplies his benefits, and beyond the worth of the contender's labours he bestows as much as it befits God to give: God who does not count out his gifts meanly, who gives greatly and with understanding enlarges his own graces, upon those who, as far as they were able, have shown by despising the earthen vessel (2 Corinthians 4:7) a love for him with the whole soul.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. I, after the address); the old English was a digest; it kept most clauses but in a broken, word-for-word order, lost the sense of the 'if' clause that conditions the weight of glory, and cited Romans 8:18 twice and 2 Corinthians 4:17 not at all.
Read ἡ ἐπ᾽ ἐλπίδι ἐλπίς, “the hope upon hope”.
Read ἀποκαλοῦντες, διαλέκτου, ὅτι (OCR ὅτε), ὠνούμεθα, ἀποκαλύπτεσθαι, τοῖς μὴ (OCR μὲ) βαρουμένοις, περιεστηκότων, ἡγεμονικόν (OCR 'ἢ; ἐμονικόν'), νομίμως, δωρουμένου, ἑαυτοῦ, καταπεφρονηκέναι.
The 'if' clause conditions κατεργάζεται: the affliction works glory for us provided we turn the mind from present pain; rendered “That holds if...”.
“who does not count out his gifts meanly”: the verb is to haggle or be stingy in reckoning.

source_text: ᾿Αλλὰ καὶ εἰ φαυλίζοιεν ἡμᾶς καὶ ἐξευτελίζοιεν ἤτοι ἀσεβεῖς ἢ μωροὺς ἀποχαλοῦντες οἱ ἀλλότριοι τῆς κατὰ τὰς ἁγίας γραφὰς διαλέχτου, ὑπομιμνησκώμεϑα ὅτε ἡ „er ἐλπίδι" ἐλπὶς, ἡ ,ἔτε μικρὸν" ἀποδοϑησομένη ἡμῖν, ἀποδοϑησεται ,διὰ φαυλισμὸν χειλέων, διὰ γλώσσης ἑτέρας". καὶ τίς οὐχ ἂν προσδέχοιτο »ϑλῖψιν ἐπὶ ϑλίψει"ς, ἵνα εὐϑέως προσδέξηται καὶ ,ἐλπίδα ἐπ᾽ ἐλπίδι", λογισάμενος μετὰ Παύλου (ὅτι οὐκ ἄξια τὰ παϑήματα τοῦ νῦν καιροῦ“, ὧν ὡσπερεὶ ὠνούίμεϑα τὴν μακαριότητα. «πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν" ἐποχαλύπτεσϑαι εἰς ἡμᾶς“ ἀπὸ τοῦ ϑεοῦ᾽ καὶ μάλιστα ἐπεὶ «τὸ παραυτίκα ἐλαφρὸν τῆς ϑλίψεως ἡμῶν", ,ἐλαφρὸν" τοῖς μὲ βαρουμένοις ὑπὸ τῶν περιεστηχότων καὶ τυγχάνον καὶ λεγόμενον, ὁσῳ πλεῖον ὑπερβάλλον γίνεται, τοσούτῳ μεῖζον xal πλεῖον βάρος αἰωνίου δόξης κατεργάζεται ἡμῖν", εἰ παρὰ τὸν καιρὸν τῶν ϑλιβόντων καὶ ὡσπερεὶ πιέζειν τὰς ψυχὰς ἡμῶν ἐθελόντων ἀποστρέψαντες τὸ ἢ; ἐμονικὸν ἡμῶν ἀπὸ τῶν ἐπιπόνων σκοποῖμεν οὐ τὰ ἐνεστηκότα ἐπίπονα ἀλλὰ τὰ διὰ τὴν ἐν τούτοις ὑπομονὴν τοῖς νομίμως" ἐν Χριστῷ ἀϑλησασι χάριτι ϑεοῦ ἀποκείμενα, πολλαπλασιάζοντος τὰς εὐεργεσίας καὶ ὑπὲρ τὴν ἀξίαν τῶν τοῦ ἀγωνισαμένου καμάτων τοσαῦτα δωρουμέγου, ὅσα ἂν πρέπῃ μὴ γλισχρολογουμένῳ διδόναι τῷ μεγαλοδώρῳ καὶ ἐπιστημόνως τὰς ἑαυτοῖ χάριτας μεγεϑύνοντι ϑεῷ ἐπὶ τοὺς ὅση δύναμις διὰ τοῦ χαταπεφρονηχέναι τοῦ ὀστρακίνου σκεύους ἐπιδειξαμένους τὴν ὅλῃ ψυχῇ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀγάπην.
